svg.data-title: T.S. of an artery and a vein

g.data-info: The outer layer of tough collagen connective tissue that anchors the artery and stops it over-stretching.
A thick layer of smooth muscle that contracts to narrow the artery and helps it cope with high blood pressure.
Wavy elastic fibres in the artery wall stretch as each surge of blood arrives, then recoil to smooth the flow.
The innermost lining: a single smooth layer of endothelial cells that reduces friction with the blood.
The narrow, round central channel that carries blood away from the heart at high pressure.
The outer collagen layer, which forms the thickest part of a vein wall.
A thin layer of smooth muscle and few elastic fibres, because blood in veins is at low pressure.
The smooth endothelial lining of the vein.
The wide, often irregular channel that returns blood to the heart at low pressure.
